Oil was found offshore of Cabinda, the small Angolan exclave north of the Congo river, by Gulf Oil in 1966, and oil became the main source of Angola's income.

Cabinda, ruled by Portugal under a treaty of 1885, has a separatist movement, FLEC, which claims it was never part of Angola. Oil from its waters, guarded by Cuban troops in the 1980s while American firms ran the wells, paid for the government side of the civil war.

After the war, deep-sea fields made Angola one of the two largest oil producers in Africa, and Luanda one of the world's most expensive cities. The wealth was concentrated in the circle of dos Santos, while most Angolans stayed poor, a pattern seen in Equatorial Guinea and in Angola.
sum: Oil was found offshore of Cabinda, the small Angolan exclave north of the Congo river, by Gulf Oil in 1966, and oil became the main source of Angola's income.
